prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System: decision support for wildland-urban interface; time sync, health checks, audit of assignment/staging changes; favors command continuity over automation when degraded. Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): primary UI; triage cases; Airspace Restricted State (helitack shows boundary, needs confirmation); produces Crew Staging Pin; promotes fire location for aviation review; records assignment packages; flags assignments on Confirmed Ignition State change. Disconnected mode: last sync shown, cached review, queued updates, no irreversible releases. Conflicts held for Redtail. Access: named accounts, RBAC, MFA; auth offline: expiring signed credentials, supervisor review later. Least privilege per actor; admin config changes separately approved, never via field accounts. Security events go to append-only audit store (time, user, device, network, record, outcome); field components buffer signed records, forward unmodified. North Lookout Camera Mast: Thermal Spot Snippet, smoke bearing. South Lookout Camera Mast: bearing track, Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier Module. Both: heartbeat/temperature/storage/pointing telemetry. Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket, readiness; never authorizes crew movement. Drone Tasking Service: Kestrel missions, status pending/active/complete; not flight-release authority; degraded comms: validates Drone Corridor Permit before automated task. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): advisory scores, perimeter, hazards; applies Ridge Shadow Mask; exposure refresh needs valid recon/weather; keeps last approved model; rejects unsigned/unversioned packages. Smoke Classifier Module: Ridge Shadow Mask; never sole basis for aircraft commitment; advisory if a mast down or image quality low. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin, exposure flags, local cache. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback relay; queues acks ≥15 min on backhaul loss. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt. East Retardant Loading Pump: Retardant Batch Slip to Tanker Base Manager; metered recirculation mode. West Retardant Loading Pump: shift-change inspection. Maintenance records required before status change. Crewline Mobile Tablet: assignments, cached staging; encrypted update queue; conflicts keep author/device/server times. Actors: County Emergency Liaison (permit; view-only), Duty Detection Officer (Orion), Air Attack

Document units:
S197: Operational records that support command decisions and safety reviews shall be retained for the incident record period defined by agency policy, while high-volume raw sensor data may follow a shorter approved retention schedule.
S198: The system shall protect retained data with encryption at rest, controlled export procedures, and deletion workflows that require documented authorization.
S199: For incidents lasting multiple operational periods, spare power, replacement network equipment, field cleaning supplies, and documented recovery procedures shall be staged so that no single equipment fault stops detection or suppression-support operations.
S200: Training for the Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System shall be completed before each fire season and refreshed whenever operating procedures or field configurations change.
S201: The training program shall be role based so that each participant practices the decisions, system functions, communications, and safety constraints that apply to the assigned position.
S202: The Duty Detection Officer shall be trained to operate the Caldera Incident Command Portal, review detections, validate confidence indicators, and escalate suspected ignitions according to the approved incident workflow.
S203: Camera familiarization shall cover the North Lookout Camera Mast and the South Lookout Camera Mast, including normal image behavior, degraded visibility conditions, routine inspection cues, and reporting of equipment faults.
S204: The Duty Detection Officer shall also learn how the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine and the Smoke Classifier Module present uncertainty so that human confirmation remains part of every operational decision.
S205: The Drone Pilot Operator shall be trained on Horizon Ridge Drone Dock procedures, Drone Tasking Service mission controls, safe launch checks, recovery actions, and loss-of-link coordination.
S206: The Air Attack Supervisor shall be trained to interpret system status during aerial operations and to coordinate with the Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console without bypassing airspace safety requirements.
S207: The Tanker Base Manager shall receive practical instruction on status entry, loading coordination, and abnormal-condition reporting for the East Retardant Loading Pump and the West Retardant Loading Pump.
S208: The Helitack Crew Leader shall be trained on use of the Crewline Mobile Tablet, field acknowledgments, location updates, and communication discipline during changing fire behavior.
S209: During field mobilization drills, the Helitack Crew Leader shall use the staging pin to confirm that the assigned crew is positioned at the exercise location.
S210: The County Emergency Liaison shall be trained to interpret public-safety information from the Caldera Incident Command Portal and to coordinate notifications with county procedures.
